summary:
Observed during SDK-PATCH-01 (.github#4935, 10.0.401 to 10.0.403, 2026-10-29/30).

1. global.json `rollForward: latestFeature` resolves to the highest installed SDK within the same major.minor (the 10.0 channel). It can therefore cross feature bands, so a 10.0.5xx SDK satisfies a 10.0.403 pin. Only `latestPatch` stays inside one band. Moving the pinned `version` raises the minimum installed SDK, not the channel.
2. An explicit FSharp.Core pin (e.g. `[10.1.401, )`) does not keep packages.lock.json stable across an SDK move. Locks restored with SDK 10.0.401 can carry that SDK's bundled library-pack FSharp.Core `contentHash` (prefix `IGqjL9U8`). Once the SDK no longer bundles that version, restore takes the nuget.org package and records its different hash (prefix `/lvOK51`) for the same version. The FsQuint fix changed exactly one `contentHash` line per lock and left version and requested range unchanged (FsQuint#47, squash d4578f2c).

How to apply: before an SDK move, grep every packages.lock.json for the outgoing SDK's bundled FSharp.Core hash, even in repositories that pin FSharp.Core explicitly. Regenerate cold with the target SDK and an isolated NuGet cache, and review that only the expected contentHash/version lines changed. Repositories whose locks already carry the nuget.org hash need no lock change; Audio, Net and Governance did not.

Limits: only hash prefixes are recorded. The bundled-versus-nuget.org selection mechanism is stated from the FsQuint commit message and the observed diffs, not derived from nupkg bytes. Projects whose locks resolve a newer bundled FSharp.Core version show a different library-pack hash; this record does not enumerate those cases.
title: An exact-pinned .NET SDK band move changes FSharp.Core lock contentHash even when FSharp.Core is explicitly pinned
